answer.program_planned_benchmark: No HumanEval/SWE-bench/GSM8K/LiveCodeBench corpus is named on this tree. The live planned evaluation is G-1 over WORK-UNIT-CATALOG.json.

which_would_be_vulnerable.reason: Measure re-runs named probes; reciting SUCCESS:UNIT from training data cannot satisfy G-1.
The catalog is a public static artifact. Timeline analysis (Roberts) would treat post-crawl model training as contaminated for any memorization test on catalog text.
Jacovi/Sainz-class n-gram leakage plus Roberts cutoff. This program has not yet named which public suite it will adopt (RES-0093).

applied_result.vulnerability: G-1 re-runs probes, so reciting a completion sentinel from training data cannot satisfy the measure (cloud ok=true is explicitly not delivery). The catalog file itself is a public static artifact: if later scored as a memorization/Q-A test without live probes, it is timeline-vulnerable once crawled. Unique-canary FPR on the clean boilerplate control is 0; extra prompt-surface hits outside the planted fixture must stay 0.
applied_result.why_this_benchmark: This tree has no published HumanEval/SWE-bench/GSM8K suite. The only evaluation this program actually runs is G-1: live named probes over catalog work units. That is the planned (and live) benchmark set on this worktree.

claims.claim: Three detector families named in the unit question (canary, held-out perturbation, timeline) each have at least one paper with an effect size AND a baseline.
Only detectors with a measured or exact FPR may disqualify a result. On this record that is Oren (0.05-by-construction) and local-canary-g1 (FPR=0.0).
A headline without a baseline is E3 and cannot promote. Probe1 rejects e3-headline-only-control when may_promote=true.
This program's live G-1 benchmark is not defeated by training-data memorization of completion sentinels.
The strongest locally runnable detector (unique canary) was applied to this program's G-1 surface: planted fires, clean is silent, extra prompt hits = 0.

detector_table.baseline: Same 1.4B model, 1-duplication injections stay above 0.05 (BoolQ dup=1: permutation p=0.099, sharded p=0.156; HellaSwag dup=1: permutation p=0.485, sharded p=0.478)
detector_table.caveat: Requires token likelihoods and an exchangeable item order. Cannot run on this worktree (no model logprob endpoint). Fails open on non-exchangeable sets (authors heuristically filter MMLU subsets).
detector_table.effect_size: MNLI 1000 examples injected 10 times: permutation p=0.009, sharded p=1.96e-11
detector_table.fpr_note: Type I error equals the chosen significance level under the exchangeability null (no contamination => all orderings equally likely). Not an empirically fitted FPR on a foreign corpus.
detector_table.name: Canonical-order vs shuffled-order likelihood (permutation / sharded rank)
detector_table.section_or_figure: Table 1 (controlled 1.4B Wikitext injection); abstract (exact false-positive guarantees)

detector_table.baseline: Strongest reference-free baseline LOSS/PPL: AUC 0.67; TPR@5%FPR 19.3%
detector_table.caveat: Needs token probabilities. WikiMIA uses Wikipedia timestamps as ground truth; that label process does not transfer to this program's G-1 oracles. Cannot disqualify a result here.
detector_table.fpr_note: Table 5 reports TPR at FPR=5% on WikiMIA member/non-member splits. That 5% is the chosen ROC operating point on WikiMIA, not a Type I guarantee on a different benchmark. FPR for disqualifying this program's scores is UNMEASURED.
detector_table.name: Min-K% Prob (mean log-likelihood of lowest-k% tokens)
detector_table.section_or_figure: Table 1 (AUC on WikiMIA); Appendix Table 6 (TPR@5%FPR); §4.3 k=20

detector_table.baseline: ChatGPT-Cheat? strict evaluation on GPT-4: 0/14 (0.00%); Algorithm 1 ROUGE-L on GPT-3.5: 7/14 (50.00%), i.e. chance on 14 binary partition labels
detector_table.caveat: Requires querying the suspect model plus a GPT-4 judge. Safety filters made ChatGPT-Cheat? unusable on GPT-4 (0/14 strict).
detector_table.effect_size: Algorithm 2 GPT-4 ICL: 14/14 (100%) on GPT-4 partitions and 13/14 (92.86%) on GPT-3.5 partitions
detector_table.fpr_note: Table 3 is partition-level agreement with human labels, not a per-instance false-positive rate for the GPT-4 ICL judge. The judge's own FPR is UNMEASURED, so this detector cannot disqualify a result.
detector_table.name: Guided instruction completion vs general instruction (Time Travel)
detector_table.section_or_figure: Table 3 overall accuracy vs human partition labels

detector_table.baseline: Same model, post-cutoff: odds ratio 1.000 (95% CI 0.986-1.014), not significant (Table 1 After column)
detector_table.caveat: Needs dated items, a published cutoff, and a popularity proxy. This program's G-1 oracles are not Codeforces-style dated problems.
detector_table.effect_size: GPT-4 Codeforces: GitHub Presence odds ratio 1.045 (95% CI 1.039-1.051) before cutoff; prose reports ~4.5% odds increase per log GitHub Presence unit pre-cutoff
detector_table.fpr_note: This is a regression association, not a binary detector with a measured FPR. A significant pre-cutoff slope is evidence of contamination but cannot disqualify a single benchmark item.
detector_table.name: Pre/post training-cutoff pass-rate vs GitHub presence
detector_table.section_or_figure: Table 1 GPT-4 Codeforces Pass Rate; §Results GitHub Presence paragraph

detector_table.baseline: Same Table 3 TruthfulQA EM: ChatGPT 0.12, GPT-4 0.10. Fully contaminated ChatGPT ~100% EM (Figure 4). The paper explicitly says the remaining-option candidate list can be large/infinite, so a 25% 4-way chance baseline is NOT a number this paper reports and is not used here. §4.2.2 prose assigns 57% EM to ChatGPT, which matches Table 3's GPT-4 cell (0.57) not ChatGPT's (0.52); this row follows Table 3.
detector_table.caveat: Needs a multiple-choice test set. This program's G-1 oracles are not MC items.
detector_table.effect_size: Table 3 MMLU Question-Multichoice EM: ChatGPT 0.52, GPT-4 0.57; Figure 4 fine-tuned-on-MMLU ChatGPT ~100% EM
detector_table.fpr_note: Table 3 EM is not a false-positive rate. Format-learning can raise slot-guessing without item memorization. Cannot disqualify.
detector_table.name: Testset Slot Guessing (mask a wrong MC option / unlikely word)
detector_table.section_or_figure: Table 3 Question-Multichoice EM; Figure 4 (~100% after fine-tune); §4.2.2 prose

detector_table.baseline: Same model, GSM8K 100-template subset 87.0; Symbolic-M1 (one clause removed) 84.4 (±2.36). Figure 4 is qualitative on names-only vs numbers; no names-only mean is tabulated for this model, so none is cited.
detector_table.caveat: 21/25 models sit >1 stddev above the GSM-Symbolic center on the original 100 GSM8K templates — suggestive, not a disqualifier.
detector_table.fpr_note: A drop on re-instantiated items can be genuine reasoning fragility rather than contamination (authors discuss both). Using the drop as a contamination detector has UNMEASURED FPR.
detector_table.name: Symbolic template re-instantiation (names/numbers) of GSM8K items
detector_table.section_or_figure: §4.1-4.2; Figure 2 dashed GSM8K line; Appendix Table 1 Gemma2-9b-it row

detector_table.baseline: Top-n sampling ranked by raw LM perplexity: 9% memorized; temperature sampling: 3%. Among 600,000 honest generations, at least 604 (0.1%) contain memorized text
detector_table.caveat: Shows memorization exists; does not by itself disqualify a leaderboard score.
detector_table.effect_size: Best attack configuration: 67% of inspected candidates are verbatim training examples
detector_table.fpr_note: 67% is precision of ranked candidates after manual+OpenAI confirmation, not the FPR of a benchmark-contamination detector. Unique inserted canaries can have FPR near 0 if the string is not in the clean corpus; that FPR is measured locally in detector local-canary-g1, not in this paper.
detector_table.name: Training-data extraction / unique-sequence memorization

detector_table.baseline: TPR=0.0 / FPR=0.0 on clean boilerplate fixture (exact match and 3-gram overlap)
detector_table.caveat: Only disqualifies a surface that contains this unique canary. Does not detect paraphrased leakage or model-weight contamination.
detector_table.effect_size: TPR=1.0 on planted fixture (exact match and 3-gram overlap)
detector_table.fpr_note: Measured on the clean boilerplate control in this probe directory. Second signal: canary bytes present in planted file, absent in clean file.
detector_table.name: Unique planted oracle string vs boilerplate (applied to this program's G-1)

detector_table.baseline: Same Table 5 10-gram F1 = 0.000 on all three rephrased-English columns (and on rephrased-Chinese); random-detection F1 = 0.500. Same Table 2 Llama-2-13B original 5-shot MMLU 54.8.
detector_table.caveat: Needs training-set access plus a GPT-4 judge. The 85.9 figure is 0-shot after 16-epoch fine-tune on rephrased MMLU; original 54.8 is 5-shot. Shot-count is not matched.
detector_table.effect_size: LLM decontaminator F1 on MMLU rephrased-English: Algebra 0.960, Sociology 0.940, US History 0.970 (Table 5). Llama-2-13B MMLU after 16-epoch fine-tune on rephrased full prompt: 85.9 (Table 2 / Figure 1)
detector_table.fpr_note: Table 5 reports pair-classification F1, not a Type I rate for disqualifying a leaderboard score. Cannot disqualify this program's results.
detector_table.name: LLM decontaminator (embedding top-k + GPT-4 same-item judge) vs n-gram on rephrased samples
detector_table.section_or_figure: Table 5 (MMLU detection F1); Table 2 (Llama-2-13B MMLU 54.8 vs 85.9)
